content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\n## Who to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\n## Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\n## Build access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\n## Sheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

## Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

## Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

## Build access
For firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.

## Sheet
One row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.
", "id": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.

    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.

Hi PERSON_5173_NAME,

It was great speaking with you last week. We are excited about the strong
alignment between [PERSON_NAME_0854]’s long-term goals, publishing capabilities and our
hybrid-casual RPG direction along with investment in AI-powered tooling.
We’re still interested in exploring co-dev with you, and potentially even
broader collaboration.

Just wanted to check in if you had any thoughts on next steps from your
side.

Best,
Leonard
===== Wed, 3 Sep 2025 15:25:50 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_4420_EMAIL cc robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi PERSON_4420_NAME,

I’m reaching out after a recent exchange with [PERSON_NAME_41001], who noted that
our applied-AI approach looks very aligned with what you are exploring. She
asked me to reach out to you, introduce [SOURCE_ORG_0001], and see if a short
conversation would be useful.

We are kicking off a $2.5M bridge to advance our AI-driven [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine
and beta launch our Match & Slash puzzle RPG. Why this could be a strong
fit:

AI-native studio: Engine with AI at the core of design, content generation,
liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
Innovative puzzle RPG on mobile: Fast, 3D Match & Slash tuned for Western
audiences with day-one liveops.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn at roughly
$100K/month, rapid iteration and multiple shots on goal.

If this aligns with T-Accelerate’s investment thesis, could we please
book  30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks?

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, two short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

*Engine demos*
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Puzzle Engine: https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk
<https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Liveops Engine: https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q
<https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q?utm_source=chatgpt.com>

*Zombie Match 3D (US stores, still in Alpha)*
iOS: https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619
<https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619?utm_source=chatgpt.com>
Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US
<https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.calmplay.zombie&hl=en_US&utm_source=chatgpt.com>

If you cannot access the builds, I can share testflight access.
Best,
Leonard
Co-founder & CEO, [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
===== Thu, 11 Sep 2025 19:56:38 +0800 | PERSON_4420_NAME <PERSON_4420_EMAIL> -> leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> cc PERSON_3242_NAME <PERSON_3242_EMAIL>, PERSON_5203_NAME <PERSON_5203_EMAIL>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: Bridge Round for [SOURCE_ORG_0001]?
Hi Leonard,

Thank you for sending over the information about [SOURCE_ORG_0001]. I apologize
for the slight delay in my response, as I've been on a business trip for
the past few days.

I've had a chance to review the materials, and I'd like to loop in my
colleagues, Karthic and Rutik, who I believe would also find this very
interesting and relevant to our investment thesis.

We would be happy to schedule a call with you soon to discuss this further.
Please let us know your availability in the coming days.

Best,
PERSON_4420_NAME

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:

at zombies to strategize

match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],
Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.
In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).
We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.
Best,
Leonard

content.text: Now replying on Leonard's thread with the counts.

input.body:
Leonard,

The bridge send list is done, as of end of day Sep 30. It's in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (Google Sheet, shared with you): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1uJzmufSuDDen7v8I0r7MRII0hKTNjgP0IIGxegT5CeI/edit

Counts by group:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel. Anton Bernstein, $25K. The DocuSign Completed notice came in Sep 26 for the re-sent $25K SAFE.
- In talks: 8 firms, 0 angels. NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, Brightwater Games Fund, a16z, SciPlay, GFR Fund and Homa. NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu and Brightwater have iOS and Android build access per Arthur's ZOM-567 log. The other four have none.
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels. Makers, Raine, BBQ Capital, General Catalyst, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Treo VC, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Triptyq, Turkven and Harlem Capital.
- Keep warm: 2 firms, 0 angels. LVP and Hiro Capital.

Everyone else stays off. That includes Paul Heydon, who backed out Sep 30 without a call or a signed SAFE. It also includes Play Ventures, Grishin, Lakestar and 1AM Gaming/March, which all passed without a call. Mattel is off too, since it was RFP talks only.

On the Existing Investor Update card I added New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists. I also made 19 "F/up with ..." cards in To Do. For NCsoft I commented on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of adding a new one. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) didn't get cards because they already have calls on my calendar.

See you Monday for the review.

Fred

I've built the send list, done what Leonard asked on the Existing Investor Update card, and replied on his thread with the counts. Everything is ready for Monday's review.

**Send list:** It's a Google Sheet called "Q4 update - send list" in your Q4 2025 investor update folder, named the way the README asks, and shared with Leonard as an editor. It covers the bridge round as of end of day Sep 30. Each row has the firm or angel, group, amount and build access.

| Group | Firms | Angels | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 | Anton Bernstein, $25K |
| In talks | 8 | 0 | NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu, Brightwater Games Fund, a16z, SciPlay, GFR Fund, Homa |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 | Makers Fund, Raine, BBQ Capital, General Catalyst, Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Treo VC, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital |
| Keep warm | 2 | 0 | London Venture Partners, Hiro Capital |

- **Anton:** he cut his commitment from $40K to $25K. Leonard voided the first SAFE, and the $25K one came back completed in DocuSign on Sep 26.
- **Build access:** Arthur's tester log in Linear shows NCsoft, T-Accelerate, Dentsu and Brightwater on both TestFlight and the Play internal track. The other four firms in talks have no build access.
- **Who stays off:** Paul Heydon said yes at $50K but backed out on Sep 30, before a call or a signed SAFE. Play Ventures, Grishin, Lakestar and 1AM Gaming (the March Gaming Fund row) all passed without a call. Mattel was only ever about the Barbie RFP.

**Trello:**
- **Checklists:** I added New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists to the card, one item per firm or angel.
- **Follow-up cards:** I created 19 "F/up with …" cards in To Do. NCsoft already had a To Do card ("F/up with Anel…"), so I commented on that one instead of adding another.
- **No card needed:** Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers (Oct 8) already have calls on your calendar, so neither got a follow-up card.

**Email:** I replied on Leonard's Sep 30 thread with the counts above. It went to Leonard only, because the reply didn't pick up Robert and Arthur from his cc line. Forward it to them if you want them to see it.

Three calls Leonard may want to check on Monday:
- **Homa (In talks):** the Sep 18 call was mainly about co-dev. I included Homa because Leonard pitched the seed extension alongside it, which his rules count.
- **Treo VC (Awaiting reply):** they contacted us first; I counted Leonard sending them the deck on Sep 4 as our outreach.
- **General Catalyst (Awaiting reply):** Leonard's email to them bounced, but Ibrahim (IH) reached out separately on Sep 12.

Files are in Fred's Q4 2025 investor update folder:
- Q4 update - send list
